rules.events: Capitals, dynasties, national milestones and changes to the province map, each with a sentence from the cited Wikipedia article that states its date.
rules.date: ISO 8601 as precise as the source: 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Years before the common era use astronomical numbering ('-0256' = 257 BCE); `year` is the same number as an integer.
rules.position: x, y (map units) only for an event bound to one place, from the coordinates of that place's Wikipedia article; events about the whole country have none.
rules.legend: Dates before about 1000 CE follow tradition and chronicles (e.g. the Hùng kings); the text says so.

events.title: Văn Lang, capital at Phong Châu (legendary)
events.text: By tradition the third Hùng dynasty named the kingdom Văn Lang with its capital at Phong Châu (date is legendary, 2524 BC).
events.evidence: Starting from the third Hùng dynasty since 2524 BC, the kingdom was renamed Văn Lang, and the capital was set up at Phong Châu

events.title: An Dương Vương founds Âu Lạc, capital Cổ Loa
events.text: An Dương Vương conquered Văn Lang and founded Âu Lạc around 257 BCE, building Cổ Loa as his seat.
events.evidence: Subsequently, he invaded Văn Lang and founded the state of Âu Lạc in approximately 257 BCE, proclaiming himself King An Dương (An Dương Vương).

events.title: Âu Lạc falls to Nanyue
events.text: An Dương Vương died after the war with Nanyue in 179 BCE.
events.evidence: An Dương Vương fled and committed suicide after the war with Nanyue forces in 179 BCE.

events.title: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh founds Đại Cồ Việt, capital Hoa Lư
events.text: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh established Đại Cồ Việt and moved the capital to Hoa Lư.
events.evidence: In 968, Đinh Bộ Lĩnh established the kingdom of Đại Cồ Việt, relocated the capital to his home in Hoa Lư.

events.title: Đinh dynasty ends; Lê Hoàn takes the throne
events.text: Đinh Toàn ceded the throne to Lê Hoàn in 980.
events.evidence: It was founded in 968 when Đinh Bộ Lĩnh vanquished the upheavals of Twelve warlords and ended when the son of Đinh Bộ Lĩnh, Đinh Toàn, ceded the throne to Lê Hoàn in 980.

events.title: Lý dynasty founded
events.text: Lý Công Uẩn succeeded Lê Long Đĩnh and founded the Lý dynasty.
events.evidence: In 1009, Công Uẩn succeeded Lê Long Đĩnh of the Lê family, thereby founding the Lý dynasty.

events.title: Capital moved to Thăng Long
events.text: Lý Thái Tổ moved the capital from Hoa Lư to the Đại La Citadel, naming it Thăng Long.
events.evidence: In 1010, Lý Thái Tổ, the first ruler of the Lý dynasty, moved the capital of Đại Việt to the site of the Đại La Citadel.

events.title: Tây Đô citadel built
events.text: Hồ Quý Ly built the Tây Đô citadel (Citadel of the Hồ dynasty) in Thanh Hóa.
events.evidence: The citadel was built in 1397.

events.title: Hồ Quý Ly founds the Hồ dynasty
events.text: Hồ Quý Ly deposed the last Trần ruler and declared himself emperor.
events.evidence: Prince An "reigned" for one year until Hồ Quý Ly deposed him in 1400 and declared himself to be the new emperor.

events.title: Ming conquest ends the Hồ dynasty
events.text: The Ming dynasty conquered the Hồ dynasty.
events.evidence: The Hồ dynasty was conquered by the Chinese Ming dynasty in 1407.

events.title: Lê Lợi founds the Lê dynasty
events.text: Lê Lợi was enthroned after driving out the Ming army.
events.evidence: The dynasty officially began in 1428 with the enthronement of Lê Lợi after he drove the Ming Chinese army from Vietnam.

events.title: Tây Sơn capital at Phú Xuân
events.text: After his coronation, Emperor Quang Trung kept Phú Xuân (Huế) as the Tây Sơn capital.
events.evidence: Ở năm 1788, Sau khi chính thức lên ngôi Hoàng đế, ông vẫn chọn Phú Xuân là kinh đô của nhà Tây Sơn.

events.title: Lê dynasty ends
events.text: The Lê dynasty ended when the Tây Sơn defeated both the Trịnh and the Nguyễn.
events.evidence: The Lê dynasty officially ended in 1789, when the peasant uprising of the Tây Sơn brothers defeated both the Trịnh and the Nguyễn, ironically in order to restore power to the Lê dynasty.

events.title: Nguyễn dynasty; capital moved to Huế
events.text: Gia Long founded the Nguyễn dynasty and moved the capital to Huế.
events.evidence: When the Nguyễn dynasty was established in 1802, Gia Long moved the capital to Huế.

events.title: Thăng Long renamed Hà Nội
events.text: Emperor Minh Mạng renamed the city Hà Nội.
events.evidence: In 1831, the Nguyễn king Minh Mạng renamed it Hà Nội (河內).

events.title: French-Spanish attack on Đà Nẵng
events.text: A Franco-Spanish fleet attacked Đà Nẵng, opening the French conquest.
events.evidence: On 1 September 1858, a Franco-Spanish fleet of fourteen warships and 3,000 expeditionary troops, led by General Charles Rigault de Genouilly, launched attacks on Vietnamese positions in Danang.

events.title: Treaty of 1862 cedes three southern provinces
events.text: Emperor Tự Đức signed a treaty granting France three southern provinces.
events.evidence: This four-year campaign resulted in Emperor Tự Đức signing a treaty in June 1862, granting the French sovereignty over three provinces in the South.

events.title: France annexes western Cochinchina
events.text: France annexed the three southwestern provinces to form Cochinchina.
events.evidence: The French annexed the three southwestern provinces in 1867 to form Cochinchina.

events.title: Treaty of Huế (Patenôtre)
events.text: The protectorate treaty placed Annam and Tonkin under France.
events.evidence: The Treaty of Huế or Protectorate Treaty (Vietnamese: Hòa ước Giáp Thân 1884, or Hòa ước Patenotre, or Hòa ước Patơnốt) was concluded on 6 June 1884 between France and Đại Nam (Vietnam/Nguyễn dynasty).

events.title: French Indochina formed
events.text: Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia were grouped into French Indochina.
events.evidence: In 1887, Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin, and the French Protectorate of Cambodia were grouped together to form French Indochina.

events.title: End of the Nguyễn monarchy
events.text: Bảo Đại's short-lived Empire of Vietnam lasted until 25 August 1945.
events.evidence: Backed by Imperial Japan, in 1945 the last Nguyễn emperor Bảo Đại abolished the protectorate treaty with France and proclaimed the Empire of Vietnam for a short time until 25 August 1945.

events.title: Declaration of Independence at Ba Đình
events.text: Hồ Chí Minh read the Declaration of Independence in Hà Nội.
events.evidence: The Declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (Vietnamese: Tuyên ngôn độc lập Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa) was written by Hồ Chí Minh and announced to the public at Ba Đình Square in Hanoi on 2 September 1945.

events.title: Geneva Conference ends; partition at 17th parallel
events.text: The Geneva Conference closed and Vietnam was provisionally divided at the 17th parallel.
events.evidence: It took place in Geneva, Switzerland, from 26 April to 21 July 1954.

events.title: Fall of Saigon
events.text: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, ending the war.
events.evidence: Saigon, the capital of South Vietnam, was captured by North Vietnam on 30 April 1975.

events.title: Northern province mergers (e.g. Hà Sơn Bình)
events.text: The National Assembly merged Hà Tây and Hòa Bình into Hà Sơn Bình, one of several northern mergers.
events.evidence: Ngày 27 tháng 12 năm 1975, Quốc hội ban hành Nghị quyết về việc thành lập tỉnh Hà Sơn Bình trên cơ sở hợp nhất tỉnh Hà Tây và tỉnh Hòa Bình.

events.title: 38 merged provinces
events.text: After the 1975-76 mergers Vietnam had 38 province-level units.
events.evidence: Đến cuối năm 1976, Việt Nam có 38 đơn vị hành chính cấp tỉnh, gồm 35 tỉnh và 3 thành phố trực thuộc trung ương.

events.title: Reunification: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
events.text: North and South Vietnam merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
events.evidence: On 2 July 1976, North and South Vietnam were merged to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

events.title: Saigon–Gia Định renamed Hồ Chí Minh City
events.text: Saigon–Gia Định was officially named Hồ Chí Minh City.
events.evidence: Ngày 2 tháng 7 năm 1976, chính thức đặt tên thành phố Sài Gòn – Gia Định là Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.

events.title: Central provinces split (Nghĩa Bình, Phú Khánh, Bình Trị Thiên)
events.text: Nghĩa Bình, Phú Khánh and Bình Trị Thiên were split; 44 province-level units by end of 1989.
events.evidence:
Ngày 30 tháng 6 năm 1989:

Chia tỉnh Nghĩa Bình thành 2 tỉnh mới lấy tên là tỉnh Quảng Ngãi và tỉnh Bình Định.

events.title: 1991 splits; Hà Tây re-established
events.text: Hà Sơn Bình, Nghệ Tĩnh, Hoàng Liên Sơn, Hà Tuyên and Gia Lai–Kon Tum were split; Hà Tây returned.
events.evidence: The province was dissolved and both Hà Tây and Hòa Bình reverted into separate provinces on August 12, 1991.

events.title: 1996 splits (61 province-level units)
events.text: Eight provinces were split, bringing the total to 61.

events.title: Cần Thơ, Đắk Lắk, Lai Châu split (64 units)
events.text: Cần Thơ, Đắk Lắk and Lai Châu were split, giving 64 province-level units.

events.title: Hà Tây merged into Hà Nội
events.text: Hà Tây province was merged into Hà Nội.
events.evidence: The merger took place on August 1, 2008.

events.title: Huế becomes a centrally governed city
events.text: Thừa Thiên Huế province became the centrally governed city of Huế.
events.evidence: Ngày 1/1/2025, tỉnh Thừa Thiên – Huế được lên cấp thành thành phố trực thuộc trung ương lấy tên là thành phố Huế, cả nước có 57 tỉnh và 6 thành phố.

events.title: Resolution 202/2025/QH15 on provincial mergers
events.text: The National Assembly passed Resolution 202/2025/QH15 merging the provinces.
events.evidence: Ngày 12 tháng 6 năm 2025, Quốc hội ban hành Nghị quyết số 202/2025/QH15 về việc sắp xếp đơn vị hành chính cấp tỉnh (nghị quyết có hiệu lực từ ngày 12 tháng 6 năm 2025).

events.title: 63 provinces become 34
events.text: Vietnam merged 63 provinces into 34 and abolished the district level.
events.evidence: On 1 July 2025, Vietnam implemented its most extensive administrative reform in decades, merging 63 provinces and cities down to 34 first-level subdivisions and eliminating the district level entirely.
